name: Notre-Dame de Paris
_about: NOTRE-DAME DE PARIS, the Gothic cathedral as its structure: the `basilica` part lays out the arcade and the aisle wall as two lines down the nave and round the five-sided apse, stands a compound pier at every node, vaults every bay -- nave, crossing, transept arms, aisles, the trapezoids of the ambulatory and the apse's fan -- on ribs springing from vaulting shafts, and props the high vault with a flying buttress and pinnacle at every node of the aisle wall, round the chevet as down the flanks; the west front in three TIERS (three portals, the great rose between lancets, the gallery) under its two flat-topped towers; the transept's ends with their roses over portals; and on the crossing the flèche, the `domed-tower` component with a 28m tent; across the west front above the portals, the Gallery of Kings: twenty-eight limestone kings of Judah on their ledge under a canopy.

params._naveW: the nave's and the aisles' clear widths, between the walls' faces
params._arcadeH: the heights the furnishing is laid out to (the organ, the gallery)
params._towerBays: the aisles' last bays at the west end, which the towers stand over: they have no aisle vault or roof of their own
params._towerD: a tower's depth: over the aisle bays it stands on and the west front's 3m -- its back is the next bay's transverse arch
params._crossA: the first of the two bays the crossing spans, from the west (the crossing square: two bays by the nave's width)
params._flyerStages: Notre-Dame's flyers clear both aisles in one leap (rebuilt so in the 1220s); Cologne's in two, from intermediate piers
params._clerSpring: the high vault springs this far over the clerestory sill: Notre-Dame's tall clerestory

church._about: nave, crossing, transept, apse and ambulatory as one vaulted skeleton: piers, arches, rib vaults, buttresses, flyers, roofs

west front._about: the west front between the towers, in three tiers: the central portal; the great rose; the open gallery

towers._about: the two towers, from the ground: a portal in the front, a window, a blind stage, then the belfry's lancet pairs; the back an arch across the aisle

tower stairs._about: the stair up each tower (`tower-stair`): the spiral turret against the outer flank, from the aisle to the terrace on top, which is the floor round its head

front courses._about: the string courses across the whole front

fleche._about: the flèche: a slender octagonal lantern and spire over the crossing -- the domed-tower component with a very tall tent

west gallery._about: the organ loft: a gallery across the nave's west bay, the doors passing under it

seating._about: the nave's seating between the arcades, from under the gallery up to the crossing, on a middle aisle

altar._about: the high altar just east of the crossing

organ._about: the great organ on the west gallery, its pipes facing east down the nave

gallery of kings ledge._about: the ledge the kings stand on, across the whole west front

gallery of kings arcade 1._about: the pointed arcade over the kings

central tympanum._about: the tympanum filling the arch's head, carved in the real one, over its lintel
